newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel eases closure imposed on self-rule areas.
newsitem.headline: Israel eases closure imposed on self-rule areas.

text.p: Thousands of Palestinian workers returned to their jobs in Israel on Sunday when the Jewish state eased a closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Palestinian Brigadier-General Saeb al-Ajez, security commander in the northern Gaza Strip, said that of the 15,000 Gaza Strip workers allowed to work in Israel, 8,000 left at dawn to return to jobs in the Jewish state.

He said that before last month's total closure, about 20,300 Palestinian workers from the West Bank had been given permits to work in Israel. But it was difficult to know how many had entered Israel after the closure was eased.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said on Saturday the closure would be eased on Sunday at 4 a.m. (0200 GMT) and entry would be permitted to 35,000 who were married and over the age of 30.
The spokeswoman said the Karni crossing between Israel and Gaza would be open to imports and exports without restriction.

Israel sealed off the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank in 1994 after the arrival of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to self-rule areas. This closure was never lifted entirely but eased intermittently.
A total closure was reimposed in February in the midst of suicide bombings by Moslem militants opposed to the peace process. The bombings in Israel killed 59 people.
Palestinians assail the closures as collective punishment and suffocating to an already struggling Palestinian economy.
